rule: Features are only ever added, or have passes flipped to true with evidence recorded in PROGRESS.md. Never delete, reword or weaken a feature once this file is committed.

features.title: Handle rules: one shared normalize-and-validate function
acceptance: Vitest (pnpm test): normalizeHandle lowercases and drops every character outside a-z, 0-9 and '-': 'Mara_Studio!' -> 'marastudio', 'MARA' -> 'mara', ' ma ra ' -> 'mara', 'mará' -> 'mar', 'a.b' -> 'ab'. It never truncates.
validateHandle returns 'short' for 0-2 characters ('', 'ab', 'a-') and this check runs before every other rule.

validateHandle returns 'ok' for exactly 30 characters ('a' x 30) and for 3-character values ('abc', 'a-b', '123'), and 'too_long' for 31 characters. The 30-character cap is a build assumption (the docs set no maximum; a DNS label allows 63), so it is asserted explicitly here.

validateHandle returns 'invalid' for a leading or trailing dash ('-mara', 'mara-') and for any value starting 'xn--' ('xn--pple-43d'), because punycode labels render as lookalike Unicode names (phishing risk on open signup). 'ma-ra' is 'ok'.

The module has no server-only imports: a Vitest test imports it in a jsdom environment (as the client signup form will) and in a node environment (as server actions will) with no error. Reserved and taken are not decided here, because the browser cannot read reserved_handles; the availability endpoint feature covers them.

features.title: Handle availability endpoint (available, reserved, taken, short, too long, invalid)
acceptance: GET http://app.localhost:3000/api/handles/check?handle=mara returns 200 with JSON {handle: 'mara', status: 'taken'} (mara is the seeded tenant).

?handle=www, ?handle=app, ?handle=api and ?handle=ADMIN return status 'reserved' (the value is normalized first, so ADMIN comes back as handle 'admin'); the reserved set comes from the reserved_handles table, not a hard-coded list.

?handle=ab, ?handle= and a missing handle param return 'short'; 31 'a' characters return 'too_long'; ?handle=-mara and ?handle=xn--pple-43d return 'invalid'; ?handle=zq-avail-1 returns 'available'. Precedence is short, too_long, invalid, reserved, taken.
Live data: after a pages row with handle 'zq-avail-1' is inserted with the secret key, the same request returns 'taken'; after that row is deleted it returns 'available' again.
Response contains only the keys handle and status, has Cache-Control: no-store, and POST returns 405.

Abuse case (direct PostgREST, publishable key): GET {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/reserved_handles?select=* with no JWT and again as a signed-in authenticated user returns 401/403 or an empty array; GET /rest/v1/pages?select=handle returns only the caller's own rows (empty for no JWT and for a user with no page). The endpoint is the only route to availability and leaks nothing beyond the status.
Host scoping: http://mara.localhost:3000/api/handles/check?handle=zz and http://localhost:3000/api/handles/check?handle=zz both return 404.

Submitting e2e-login-1@example.com replaces the form with a sent state: heading 'Check your email', text 'We emailed a sign-in link to e2e-login-1@example.com.', a 'Use a different email' button (returns to the form, field cleared and focused) and a 'Resend link' button that is disabled with a countdown ('Resend in 60s', verified with page.clock) and enabled at 0. The email: subject 'Your HYDLNK sign-in link'; HTML and plain-text parts; one primary link labelled 'Sign in to HYDLNK' whose href starts with http://app.localhost:3000/auth/callback and is not a supabase.co verify URL; body says the link works once and expires in 1 hour, plus 'If you didn’t ask for this, ignore this email.'; no exclamation marks; the HTML has no fixed width above 600px and the link button is at least 44px tall.

features.title: Auth callback signs in from the emailed link in any browser
acceptance: Opening the emailed link in the same Playwright context ends on http://app.localhost:3000/ (default landing; routed onward by the auth gate feature) with a session cookie set; GET {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/user with that cookie's access token returns the signed-in email, and a reload keeps the session.

Opening a second fresh link in a brand-new browser context (no cookies, simulating a phone mail app that opens a different browser than the one that requested the link) also signs in. This requires the token-hash style link from the login feature's template verified by the callback, not a PKCE code-verifier cookie.

A link that was already used and a link with one character of its token altered both end on http://app.localhost:3000/login?error=link_invalid showing 'That sign-in link expired or was already used. Request a new one.' above the email form: HTTP 200, no session cookie set, no 500. Vitest: the callback maps the verify errors otp_expired and invalid token to that same redirect.
GET http://app.localhost:3000/auth/callback with no parameters redirects to /login.

Open-redirect abuse: a valid callback URL with an added next=https://evil.example, next=//evil.example, next=/\evil.example, next=javascript:alert(1) or redirect_to=https://evil.example always ends on http://app.localhost:3000/. No request parameter ever controls the destination.
/auth/callback is served on the app host only; http://localhost:3000/auth/callback and http://mara.localhost:3000/auth/callback return 404.

Test helper for every later signed-in spec: a Playwright fixture signInAs(email) creates the user if needed, generates a sign-in link with the secret key (Supabase auth admin generateLink), opens it through /auth/callback and saves storageState, so later specs sign in without reading the inbox. A smoke spec proves it yields a signed-in session for the seeded user mara in both Playwright projects.

features.title: Account row is created server-side on first sign-in
acceptance: After a brand-new address (e2e-acct-1@example.com) completes the callback, exactly one accounts row exists with id equal to that auth user's id, plan 'free', stripe_customer_id null and suspended_at null (read with the secret-key client).

Idempotent: sign out, request and open another link for the same address and there is still exactly one row with unchanged values (a plan set to 'pro' with the secret key is not reset). Two concurrent calls of the ensure-account function for one user produce one row and no error (Vitest integration).
Self-healing: delete that row with the secret key, then load any signed-in app page; the row is recreated with plan 'free'.
The row is written only by server-only code using the secret key, and the user id comes from the verified session, never from request input.

Abuse case (direct PostgREST, publishable key plus the user's JWT, role authenticated): POST /rest/v1/accounts with {id: <own id>, plan: 'studio'} is rejected (401/403, code 42501) and creates no row; PATCH /rest/v1/accounts?id=eq.<own id> with {plan: 'studio'}, {stripe_customer_id: 'cus_x'} and {suspended_at: null} each is rejected or updates 0 rows, with values unchanged when re-read using the secret key; DELETE /rest/v1/accounts?id=eq.<own id> is rejected or deletes 0 rows.
Read isolation: GET /rest/v1/accounts?select=* returns exactly the caller's own row, and ?id=eq.<another user's id> returns an empty array. A pgTAP file run by pnpm test:db covers the same cases.

features.title: Session cookies are host-only on the app host; auth routes exist on the app host only
acceptance: After signing in on http://app.localhost:3000, context.cookies() shows the Supabase auth cookie(s) (sb-...-auth-token...) for host app.localhost with no Domain attribute (host-only), Path=/ and SameSite=Lax.
Requests the same context makes to http://mara.localhost:3000/ and http://localhost:3000/ carry no sb- cookie in their request headers, and their responses contain no Set-Cookie header.

On http://mara.localhost:3000, /login, /signup, /claim, /auth/callback, /editor, /design, /analytics, /domains, /settings and /api/handles/check all return 404. On http://localhost:3000 the same paths return 404, except /login and /signup, which redirect (308) to the same path on http://app.localhost:3000 with the query string preserved.
Loading http://mara.localhost:3000/ and http://localhost:3000/ triggers zero requests to the Supabase auth URL: session refresh runs only for app-host requests.

Vitest on the proxy's session helper: an expired access token with a valid refresh token yields a response carrying refreshed cookies and the request proceeds as signed in; an invalid refresh token clears the cookies and the request is treated as signed out.
Persistence: a context restored from saved storageState keeps the user signed in when it loads http://app.localhost:3000/.

Abuse case: replaying a valid sb-...-auth-token value as a Cookie header on requests to http://mara.localhost:3000/ and http://localhost:3000/ changes nothing in the response (same HTML, no personalisation, no Set-Cookie), and the tenant host never accepts it as a session.

Production smoke after deploy: on https://app.hydlnk.com the auth cookie has Secure, host app.hydlnk.com and no Domain attribute, and https://hydlnk.com and https://<any handle>.hydlnk.com neither receive nor set it.

features.title: Auth gate and landing redirects for app routes
acceptance: Signed out, GET http://app.localhost:3000/, /editor, /design, /analytics, /domains, /settings and /claim each return a redirect to /login (assert status and Location header; destination pages may not exist yet); /login and /signup render.
Signed in with an account that has no page: / and each of /editor, /design, /analytics, /domains, /settings redirect to /claim; /claim renders.
Signed in with an account that has a page: / redirects to /editor; /login, /signup and /claim redirect to /editor.
Abuse case: the gate trusts verified claims, not cookie presence: a request carrying a forged sb-...-auth-token cookie that holds a garbage JWT is treated as signed out and redirected to /login.
Signed-in app responses send Cache-Control: no-store; after signing out, page.goBack() onto an app page shows /login and no cached app content.
No redirect or link ever carries a return-URL parameter: /login and /signup ignore ?next=, ?redirect_to= and ?return_to= entirely.

features.title: Server-only handle claim creates the first page (reserved, taken, plan limit, race-safe)
acceptance: claimHandle (server-only, secret key) for a signed-in account with no page inserts one pages row: owner_id equals the session user, handle is the normalized value, draft is an empty page document (blocks: [], no token overrides), published and published_at are null; it returns the handle.

Each rejection returns a typed error and writes nothing: 'short', 'too_long', 'invalid', 'reserved' (including 'WWW', 'Admin' and any value in reserved_handles), 'taken' (a pages row already has it), 'page_limit' (account already has its plan's maximum, 1 on free, even for a different handle), 'no_account', and 'suspended' (accounts.suspended_at is set). The limit follows accounts.plan: with plan 'pro' set via the secret key a second claim succeeds and a fourth is rejected; 'studio' allows 15.

Race safety: 10 parallel claims of 'zq-race-1' by 10 different accounts leave exactly one pages row, 9 'taken' results and no 500; 2 parallel claims by one free account for 'zq-r-a' and 'zq-r-b' leave exactly one row, so the page limit is enforced by the database (lock or constraint), not only an app-level count.
Case safety: with the secret key, inserting handle 'MARA' while 'mara' exists fails with a unique violation, so differently-cased duplicates cannot coexist.
The owner always comes from the verified session: a claim request whose body contains another user's owner_id ignores it; an unauthenticated call returns 401 and writes no row.

Abuse case (direct PostgREST, publishable key plus the user's JWT, role authenticated; pgTAP via pnpm test:db): POST /rest/v1/pages with {handle: 'zq-direct-1', owner_id: <own id>} is rejected (401/403, code 42501) and creates no row; the same with handle 'www' is rejected; a second page for an account that already has one is rejected; PATCH /rest/v1/pages?id=eq.<own page id> with {handle: 'zq-other'}, with {published: {}} and with {published_at: 'now'} each is rejected or updates 0 rows, values unchanged when re-read with the secret key; DELETE /rest/v1/pages?id=eq.<own page id> is rejected or deletes 0 rows; GET /rest/v1/pages?select=handle as a different user returns an empty array.

Empty or under 3 characters: neutral text 'At least 3 characters — letters, numbers and dashes.' in #5E5A54, field border #D9D6D0, and no request to /api/handles/check is sent.

After a debounce of at most 400 ms: 'mara' shows red text 'That one’s taken. Try another.' with border #B23A2B; 'www', 'app' and 'api' show red 'That name is reserved. Try another.'; '-mara' and 'xn--abc' show red 'Handles can’t start or end with a dash or start with xn--.'; 31 characters shows red 'Handles can be up to 30 characters.' (no maxlength attribute, so the state is reachable); 'zq-live-1' shows green (#2F7D4F) with a check icon and 'zq-live-1.hydlnk.com is available'.

features.title: Tenant host serves a placeholder when the handle is claimed and a 404 when it is not
acceptance: For a claimed handle whose published column is null ('zq-ph-1', claimed through the server-only claim), GET http://zq-ph-1.localhost:3000/ returns 200 HTML with <title> 'zq-ph-1.hydlnk.com', exactly one h1 'zq-ph-1', the line 'Nothing published here yet.', and <meta name='robots' content='noindex'>. (Milestone 2 swaps in the real renderer for non-null published; this milestone never renders a page document.)

It is a tenant page, not HYDLNK UI: the page root sets the tenant token CSS variables resolved from the system-default theme by the Milestone 0 token resolver, and the response contains no --hl-* custom properties, no app-shell markup (no sidebar, top bar or tab bar) and no #1C1B1A charcoal bar; the placeholder uses system fonts and makes no network request to any host other than zq-ph-1.localhost:3000 (the Google Fonts link arrives in Milestone 3 and applies only to pages rendered from a published document).

Published-only: set the page's draft to a document containing the text 'DRAFT-MARKER-7f3a' with the secret key; the response body never contains it (public render reads only published and published_at).

Abuse case, no cookies: the response has no Set-Cookie, and sending an sb-...-auth-token cookie header to this host does not change the response. /login, /signup, /claim, /editor, /settings and /auth/callback on this host all return 404. A request whose Host header is ZQ-PH-1.localhost:3000 (upper case) returns the same page.

GET http://zq-none-1.localhost:3000/ (no pages row) returns status 404 with Cache-Control: no-store and <meta name='robots' content='noindex'>. The page uses HYDLNK UI styling (background #F4F3F0, ink text), says 'This address isn’t claimed.' with a primary link 'Claim zq-none-1' to http://app.localhost:3000/signup?handle=zq-none-1 and a secondary link 'Go to hydlnk.com' to http://localhost:3000/.

features.title: Page document schema and limits in Zod
acceptance: Vitest unit: one shared module (extending the Milestone 0 page and block schemas) exports `draftDocSchema` and `publishDocSchema` for the page document `{version, rev, profile:{name, bio, photo}, theme:{ref, overrides}, blocks[]}`. The editor, the Publish action and the public-page query all import from it (static import check). `theme` reuses the Milestone 0 token types.

`draftDocSchema` is lenient about completeness so half-typed blocks can autosave (empty strings and empty URLs allowed); `publishDocSchema` is strict. Fixture: a link block with label '' and url '' passes the draft schema and fails the publish schema; a doc with an empty display name does the same.

The block union has exactly nine types: link, card, header, text, image, social, embed, grid, divider. Each block has `id` (nanoid, 8-24 chars of A-Za-z0-9_-) and `visible` (boolean, defaults true). An unknown `type` fails both schemas; unknown keys are stripped on parse so published JSON carries only known fields.

Limit table, each tested at the limit (passes) and limit+1 (fails both schemas), counted in Unicode code points with the same helper the editor counters use: display name 60, bio 160, blocks 50, link label 80, card title 60, card caption 100, header text 80, text 600, image alt 140, embed caption 80, social icons 1 to 8, grid cells 2 to 6, cell title 40, cell subtitle 60.

Ids are unique across the whole document, including social-icon ids and grid-cell ids (so Milestone 4 click tracking can resolve any link by id); a duplicate id fails both schemas. Moving, editing or re-saving a block never changes its id (round-trip test).

Text fields are trimmed. Control characters (U+0000-U+001F except newline inside text blocks, U+007F-U+009F) and bidi override or isolate characters (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) fail `publishDocSchema`.

Image references are `{path, width, height}` and `path` must match `^[0-9a-f-]{36}/[a-z0-9-]{8,64}[.](jpg|png|webp)$` (owner folder, then a file name; this one scheme covers the pass-through names of this milestone and the hashed WebP names of Milestone 5); an external URL, a path containing `..` or a data: URI fails both schemas, so a tenant cannot point the renderer at a third-party image.

Block `overrides` keep only the color, buttonStyle and radius keys the Milestone 0 resolver allows: any other key (for example `fontHeading`) is stripped on parse and never reaches `published`, while an invalid value for an allowed key (radius -5, color 'red') fails `publishDocSchema`.

`safeHref(url)` returns the normalized URL for valid input and `undefined` for anything else. It is the only function renderer code may use to obtain an href.
Table-driven test over every URL-bearing field in `publishDocSchema` (link.url, card.url, image.url, embed.url, social icon url, grid cell url): each rejects `javascript:alert(1)` and `data:` URLs.

Email addresses are not URLs: the social email icon stores an address validated by a separate `emailAddress` rule (one `@`, no whitespace, at most 254 chars); the renderer builds the `mailto:` href from it. `mailto:` is rejected by `httpUrl` everywhere else.

features.title: Page media bucket and server-only image upload
acceptance: New migration creates a public Storage bucket `page-media` (the single bucket for every tenant image from here on) with `file_size_limit` 4 MB (below Vercel's 4.5 MB request-body cap; the 10 MB figure in PLAN is the Free plan's total upload quota, enforced in Milestone 4) and `allowed_mime_types` image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp. No insert, update, delete or select policy for `anon` or `authenticated` exists on its objects, so files are readable by public URL but cannot be listed or written by clients. pgTAP covers the policies.

The one upload route is `POST http://app.localhost:3000/api/media` (multipart field `file`, plus an optional field `kind` with value avatar, background or content, default content, which Milestone 5's pipeline uses to pick an output size; any other `kind` value returns 400). It requires a session, rejects bodies over 4 MB with 413 before decoding, sniffs magic bytes (JPEG FF D8 FF, PNG 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A, WebP RIFF....WEBP) and ignores the client-declared type and file name. It stores the file as-is at `{uid}/{uuid}.{jpg|png|webp}` (uid always from the session; any owner or folder field in the form is ignored) with a one-year cache-control, and returns `{path, width, height, url}` with width and height read from the image header, valid per the image-reference schema (an 800x600 fixture returns width 800, height 600). Images wider or taller than 8000px are rejected with 422.
The public URL `{SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/public/page-media/{path}` returns 200 with the correct content-type and a long `cache-control`.

Rejected with a clear error and no object created (verified by listing with the secret key): no session (401), a PNG-named SVG or HTML file declared as image/png (415), a GIF (415), a 0-byte file (422), and a file of 4 MB + 1 byte (413).

Direct-API abuse with mara's access token and the publishable key: `POST /storage/v1/object/page-media/{mara uid}/x.png` is rejected (no client insert policy); uploading into jonas's folder is rejected; overwriting an existing object with upsert is rejected; deleting another user's object is rejected; `POST /storage/v1/object/list/page-media` as anon and as authenticated returns no objects; a 5 MB direct upload is refused by the bucket limit.

Replacing or removing an image in the editor changes only the draft reference: the client makes no Storage delete call, and an object the published copy still references stays readable at its public URL. Garbage collection of unreferenced objects is the Milestone 5 cleanup feature; resizing, WebP conversion and per-account quotas are Milestones 5 and 4.

features.title: Publish gate: server-only, validated, resolved
acceptance: Server Action `publishPage(pageId)` is `'use server'` and imports the secret-key client under `server-only`. Its signature takes only a page id and no document (type test); it reads the draft from Postgres itself. Playwright: type ' X' into Bio and click Publish within 100 ms; the live page `http://mara.localhost:3000` contains the final text (the client flushes autosave first, and the server reads the saved draft).

Auth (Vitest integration against local Supabase): no session is rejected as unauthorized; jonas calling it for mara's page id is rejected as forbidden; in both cases `pages.published` and `published_at` are unchanged.

Validation gate: the draft is parsed with `publishDocSchema` plus the URL rule and embed allowlist, every image `path` must start with the owner's uid and exist in `page-media`, and required fields must be filled. Any failure returns `{ok:false, errors:[{blockId, field, message}]}` and writes nothing. Direct-API abuse: as mara with the publishable key, PATCH `pages.draft` through PostgREST to include a link URL `javascript:alert(1)`, a `data:` URL, an embed of `https://evil.example/x`, a photo path in jonas's folder, 51 blocks and a display name with U+202E. Each Publish attempt is refused with the offending block id named, `published` stays as before and the live HTML never contains those strings.
Escaping: a display name of `<script>alert(1)</script>` is valid, publishes, and renders as escaped text (live HTML contains `<script>`, no dialog event).

Success writes `pages.published` as the publish form of the draft: the profile, only blocks with `visible !== false` (hidden blocks are removed, not just flagged), the frozen resolved tokens (see the freeze feature) and `published_at = now()`, and returns `{ok:true, publishedAt}`. Unknown draft keys are stripped.

Direct-API abuse: with mara's access token and the publishable key, PATCH `/rest/v1/pages?id=eq.{id}` with `{published: {...}}` and with `{published_at: '2026-01-01'}` are each rejected (HTTP 403 or 401, permission denied) and `published` is unchanged.

UI: the 'Publish' button shows 'Publishing...' and is disabled while running (double-click sends one request); on success a toast 'Published.' with a 'View live page' link to `http://mara.localhost:3000` appears and the status chip reads 'Published' (chip states are in the Unpublished changes feature).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the Publish button is at least 44px tall, the toast does not overlap the bottom tab bar, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide) and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.

features.title: Google Fonts allowlist and safe stylesheet URL builder
acceptance: Vitest: the allowlist module exports at least 12 families, each with a family name, a category (sans, serif, display or mono) and a non-empty list of supported weights; it includes Instrument Serif, Fraunces and Geist (the tenant fonts used in Design.dc.html), at least 3 sans and at least 3 serif families.

Vitest: the stylesheet URL builder given ['Instrument Serif','Geist'] returns one https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2 URL with exactly those two family params (URL-encoded, e.g. family=Instrument+Serif) plus display=swap; the same family passed twice is emitted once.
Vitest: given 'Comic Sans MS', '', 'Geist;}body{x:y', 'Geist, sans-serif' or a 200-character string, the builder throws or returns null, and no returned URL ever contains the raw input.

Vitest: the fontHeading and fontBody Zod schemas accept every allowlisted family and reject each invalid string above. End-to-end abuse cases (a direct draft write of a hostile font name) are asserted in the tenant fonts and Publish validation features.

features.title: Token values: strict schema and injection-safe CSS variables
acceptance: Vitest: the 8 colour tokens (bg, surface, text, textMuted, accent, buttonBg, buttonText, border) accept #RGB, #RRGGBB and #RRGGBBAA and reject 'red', 'rgb(0,0,0)', '#GGGGGG', 'url(x)', '#fff;}body{display:none' and any string longer than 9 characters.

Vitest: enum tokens accept only their documented values (buttonStyle fill|outline|soft|shadow|pill, density compact|regular|airy, bgType solid|gradient|image, align left|center, letterCase normal|uppercase|lowercase) and reject any other string.

Vitest: numeric tokens enforce ranges and reject NaN, negatives and numeric strings: radius 0-32, borderWidth 0-4, scale 0.8-1.3, weightHeading one of 400/500/600/700, maxWidth 360-720, overlayOpacity 0-1, blur 0-24.

Vitest: bgImage accepts only an https (or the local http://127.0.0.1:54321) URL under this project's Storage public path for the `page-media` bucket and rejects javascript:, data:, http: on production hosts, https://evil.example/x.png and any URL containing quotes or parentheses. The page-level overrides schema accepts any subset of token keys and rejects unknown keys such as 'fontHeadingg' or 'customCss'.

Vitest: the CSS variable serializer (extending the Milestone 2 renderer root) emits one --t-* custom property per token, and drops any value that fails the token schema, using the system default value for that token instead; values are never concatenated into a style string without validation.

Vitest: parsing the env with any one of those required variables removed throws an error that names the missing variable; with all of them present it parses.

Vitest: a STRIPE_SECRET_KEY starting sk_live_ or rk_live_ fails validation in every NODE_ENV with a message saying live keys are not allowed until the move to Vercel Pro; a key starting sk_test_ passes.

Vitest: when VERCEL_ENV=production, setting VERCEL_API_BASE_URL or STRIPE_API_HOST fails validation (API calls cannot be redirected in production); when unset they default to https://api.vercel.com and Stripe's real host.

After pnpm build, grep -r over .next/static finds none of the values of VERCEL_API_TOKEN, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CRON_SECRET or VISITOR_HASH_SECRET, and a throwaway client component that imports the Vercel client or Stripe client module makes the build fail through server-only.

features.title: Plan limits come from one table shared by TypeScript and Postgres
acceptance: Vitest: a TypeScript module exports for free/pro/studio: pages 1/3/15, custom domains 0/1/15, upload bytes 10485760/104857600/1073741824 (10 MiB, 100 MiB, 1 GiB), saved themes 3/unlimited/unlimited, analytics history days 30/365/365, and analytics breakdowns (referrer, device, country) off/on/on.

Database: the SQL function public.plan_limits(p_plan text) (the one the Milestone 0 limit triggers call; extend it in a new migration with analytics-history and breakdown columns) returns the same numbers (unlimited as null); a Vitest integration test loops over every plan and limit in the TypeScript table, calls the function on the local stack, and asserts identical values; a second test that mutates a copy of the TypeScript table proves the parity check reports a mismatch.
pgTAP: plan_limits('enterprise') raises an error (fail closed, never a default); accounts.plan rejects any value other than free, pro or studio through a check constraint.

Direct-API check: POST /rest/v1/rpc/plan_limits with the publishable key returns only the public numbers above and no per-account data; no feature in this milestone hard-codes a limit number outside this table (grep of src/ for the literals 10485760, 104857600 and 1073741824 matches only the table module).

features.title: Stripe webhook rejects anything that is not signed by Stripe
acceptance: POST http://app.localhost:3000/api/stripe/webhook (production https://app.hydlnk.com/api/stripe/webhook) with a body signed through stripe.webhooks.generateTestHeaderString and the configured STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET returns 200 with {"received":true}; verification uses the raw request body (a Vitest case that re-serialises the same JSON with different whitespace fails verification).

A request with no Stripe-Signature header, a header signed with a different secret, a body altered by one character after signing, or a timestamp older than 5 minutes returns 400 every time, and in every case the accounts table is byte-for-byte unchanged and the payload is not logged.
A validly signed event of a type the handler does not handle (for example invoice.paid) returns 200 and writes nothing; GET, PUT and DELETE on the route return 405.
Abuse case: an unsigned POST whose JSON claims a customer.subscription.updated event moving mara's customer to the Studio price returns 400 and mara's accounts.plan is still free.

The route exists only on the app host: the same signed POST to http://mara.localhost:3000/api/stripe/webhook, http://localhost:3000/api/stripe/webhook and a custom host (links.example.test, mapped to 127.0.0.1 with Chromium --host-resolver-rules or a curl Host header) returns 404 without evaluating the signature.

With stripe listen --project-name hydlnk --forward-to http://app.localhost:3000/api/stripe/webhook running, stripe trigger customer.subscription.updated --project-name hydlnk shows a 200 response in the listener output (an event for a customer we do not know is acknowledged and ignored).

features.title: Webhook writes the plan and subscription state to accounts
acceptance: Migration adds server-written columns to accounts: stripe_subscription_id, billing_interval ('month' or 'year'), current_period_end, cancel_at_period_end and stripe_event_created_at.

A signed checkout.session.completed (mode subscription, client_reference_id = account id, customer cus_test_1) sets accounts.stripe_customer_id to cus_test_1 when it is null; the plan is set by the subscription events below, not by this event.

A signed customer.subscription.created or customer.subscription.updated with status active, trialing or past_due and price STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_MONTHLY sets plan 'pro', billing_interval 'month', current_period_end, cancel_at_period_end and stripe_subscription_id; price STRIPE_PRICE_STUDIO_YEARLY sets plan 'studio' and interval 'year' (table-driven over all four price ids).

Subscription statuses canceled, unpaid, incomplete, incomplete_expired and paused set plan 'free'; a signed customer.subscription.deleted sets plan 'free' and clears the subscription columns while keeping stripe_customer_id (the portal still needs it).

The account is found by stripe_customer_id, falling back to subscription.metadata.account_id; an unknown customer returns 200 and writes nothing; an unknown price id returns 200, changes nothing and logs an error without the payload.

Idempotent and order-safe: delivering the same signed event twice leaves the row identical; a deleted event with created=200 followed by an updated event with created=100 leaves the account on free (events older than stripe_event_created_at are ignored).

Abuse case (pgTAP and curl): with a user's JWT and the publishable key, PATCH /rest/v1/accounts?id=eq.<me> setting plan, stripe_customer_id, suspended_at or any new column updates no row (permission denied or zero rows), while selecting own row still works and selecting another account's row returns nothing.

features.title: Settings & billing screen: current plan and plan cards
acceptance: Test harness: a local Stripe API stub (set through STRIPE_API_HOST) records every request (method, path, body) and returns configurable responses; all Stripe-calling tests in this milestone use it, never the real API.

Signed in on http://app.localhost:3000/settings (nav label 'Settings & billing', phone tab 'Account') the breadcrumb reads 'Account' and the h1 'Settings & billing'; a signed-out request redirects to sign-in and renders no plan data. The Account card from Milestone 1 stays on the screen below the new cards.
Free account: the charcoal band (mono uppercase label 'Current plan' with a 6px brass square) shows 'Free' at 30px/700 and '$0 · free forever' and no renewal line.

Pro on monthly with current_period_end 2026-11-01 and the stub reporting a default card ending 4242: the band shows 'Pro', '$5 / month · billed monthly' and 'Renews Nov 1, 2026 on the card ending 4242.'; yearly shows '$48 / year · billed yearly'; Studio shows '$15 / month · billed monthly'; if the stub errors, the card clause is dropped and the rest still renders; cancel_at_period_end true shows 'Ends Nov 1, 2026. You keep Pro until then.' instead.

Plans section shows three cards (Free $0, Pro $5/mo, Studio $15/mo) with blurbs derived from PLAN.md: Free '1 page, hydlnk.com address, 30 days of per-link clicks.', Pro '3 pages, 1 custom domain, a year of analytics, no badge.', Studio '15 pages, 15 custom domains, a year of analytics, no badge.'; nothing on the screen mentions editors, team access, CSV export or scheduled links (all deferred from v1).

The card matching accounts.plan shows an inert 'Current plan' tile (#EFEDE9, 1px ink ring) instead of a button; Free account: Pro and Studio show 'Upgrade to Pro' and 'Upgrade to Studio'; Pro account: Free shows 'Downgrade' and Studio shows 'Upgrade to Studio'; Studio account: Free and Pro show 'Downgrade' (what each button does is covered by the Checkout and portal features).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/settings the cards stack in one column, each card button is full width and at least 44px tall (the mockup's 40px is raised), every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide), the bottom tab bar shows 'Account' active with a 2px brass top marker, and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the 240px sidebar shows 'Settings & billing' active, the content column is capped at 920px and the three cards sit in one row.

features.title: Upgrade from Free through Stripe Checkout (sandbox)
acceptance: On a Free account at http://app.localhost:3000/settings a 'Monthly | Yearly' segmented control (role group 'Billing interval', default Monthly) switches the card prices between $5/mo and $48/yr for Pro and between $15/mo and the Studio yearly price for Studio (prices come from the plan price config; PLAN.md prices are placeholders and Studio yearly is not set yet).

Clicking 'Upgrade to Pro' on Monthly submits a server action that creates a Stripe Checkout Session in subscription mode with price STRIPE_PRICE_PRO_MONTHLY, client_reference_id and subscription_data.metadata.account_id both equal to the account id, success_url http://app.localhost:3000/settings?checkout=success and cancel_url http://app.localhost:3000/settings?checkout=canceled, Stripe API version 2026-09-30.endive, and answers 303 to the session URL (stub assertion on the request body; in the production sandbox run the browser lands on checkout.stripe.com in test mode showing the same amount as the card). A table-driven test covers all four plan and interval combinations against the four price ids.
The Stripe customer is created once and its id saved to accounts.stripe_customer_id before the session is created; starting Checkout twice reuses it (the stub sees exactly one customer-create call).

Abuse case: the action accepts only plan in {pro, studio} and interval in {month, year}; a POST with price=price_x, plan=free, plan=enterprise or interval=week returns 400 and the stub receives no session request; an unauthenticated POST returns 401 with no Stripe call; price ids and customer ids are never read from the request.

Abuse case: an account whose plan is not free gets 409 already_subscribed from the same action and no Checkout Session is created, so a second subscription cannot be started; its settings page shows no Checkout buttons.

Return handling: /settings?checkout=success shows 'Confirming your upgrade' (aria-live polite) and re-reads the account every 2 seconds for up to 30 seconds; when a signed customer.subscription.created webhook flips the plan to Pro the band changes to Pro with no manual reload; after 30 seconds without a flip it shows 'This is taking longer than usual. Refresh in a minute. You are only charged once.'

Abuse case: loading /settings?checkout=success as a Free account that never paid leaves accounts.plan 'free' and the UI on Free (the return URL never unlocks anything); /settings?checkout=canceled shows 'Checkout canceled. Your plan hasn’t changed.'
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/settings the interval control and every Upgrade button are at least 44px tall and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the control sits above the plan cards and the layout matches the Billing mockup column width.

features.title: Manage billing and plan changes through the Stripe customer portal
acceptance: A 'Manage billing' primary button (charcoal, 44px, external-link icon) appears in the plan band for any account with a stripe_customer_id, including a Free account that once subscribed, and is absent when the id is null; helper text 'Card, invoices and cancellation open in Stripe’s secure customer portal.' sits under the buttons.

Clicking it posts a server action that creates a Stripe billing-portal session for that account's customer only, with return_url on the app host /settings, and answers 303 to the portal URL (stub assertion on customer and return_url; the production sandbox run lands on billing.stripe.com).

'Switch to yearly · $48/yr' (Studio shows the yearly Studio price) appears for monthly subscribers only and creates a portal session whose flow is the subscription-update confirmation for the same subscription and the same plan's yearly price id; yearly subscribers do not see it.

'Upgrade to Studio' on a Pro account creates a portal session with a subscription-update confirmation to the Studio price at the account's current interval and never creates a Checkout Session; 'Downgrade' on the Free card opens a portal session with the subscription-cancellation flow; 'Downgrade' on the Pro card of a Studio account opens an update confirmation to the Pro price at the current interval.
Returning from the portal changes nothing in HYDLNK by itself: accounts.plan changes only when the signed webhook arrives and the page shows what the database holds.

Abuse case: the actions accept only the intents manage, switch_yearly, upgrade_studio and downgrade; customer ids and price ids are never read from the request; an unknown intent returns 400; an account with no customer id calling manage gets 409 'Nothing to manage yet.' with no Stripe call; no request can reach another account's customer.
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/settings the portal buttons are full width and at least 44px tall with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the button group sits in the right column of the plan band, max width 320px.

features.title: Badge and cached pages follow a plan change without republishing
acceptance: After a signed customer.subscription.created for the Pro price reaches /api/stripe/webhook, the very next request to http://mara.localhost:3000/ renders without the 'Made with HYDLNK' badge (the webhook calls `invalidateAccountPages(accountId)` from Milestone 2 in a route handler, using revalidateTag with immediate expiry rather than updateTag); a signed customer.subscription.deleted brings the badge back. Both are checked on the subdomain and on a custom host.
Only that account is refreshed: another account's page response stays `x-nextjs-cache: HIT` with its query counter unchanged.

The page stays static: the second request after the refresh runs no Postgres query (query log), and the badge decision still comes from accounts.plan read at render time, not from the draft or published JSON.

Abuse case: a Free user who adds hideBadge, showBadge:false or badge:false to the draft JSON through PATCH /rest/v1/pages (draft is the only writable column) and then publishes still shows the badge; an unsigned POST to the webhook claiming a Pro subscription returns 400 and the badge stays.
At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ the page without the badge shows no empty gap above the report link, with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and the badge when present is at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the badge is centred inside the page's max-width column, or absent for Pro and Studio.

features.title: Verified custom hostnames serve their page and nothing else
acceptance: With a domains row {hostname links.example.test, status verified, page_id = mara's page} and mara's page published, a request with Host links.example.test (Playwright APIRequestContext with a Host header, or a browser launched with --host-resolver-rules='MAP links.example.test 127.0.0.1' at http://links.example.test:3000/) returns 200 containing mara's published display name and the same body markup as http://mara.localhost:3000/; the address bar URL stays '/'.

Host matching ignores case, port and a trailing dot: LINKS.Example.Test:3000 and links.example.test. both resolve; the lookup reads only the real Host header, so X-Forwarded-Host and X-Original-Host naming another hostname are ignored.

Each of these returns 404 with the generic not-found page and no tenant data: a hostname with no domains row; a row with status 'pending'; a row whose page has published = null (a draft never leaks); a *.vercel.app host.
Abuse case: the internal route is unreachable directly: GET /sites/<mara page id> on localhost:3000, app.localhost:3000, mara.localhost:3000 and links.example.test returns 404.

On a custom host only the page, its OG image, /r/*, /api/e and static assets are served: /login, /signup, /settings, /domains, /analytics, /auth/callback, /api/stripe/webhook and /anything-else return 404, and no response carries Set-Cookie even when the request sends an sb-* cookie; a Vitest proxy test shows /r/* and /api/e are left unrewritten (the handlers arrive in the analytics features).
Metadata on the custom host: og:url and og:image are absolute URLs on links.example.test and the og:image URL returns 200 image/png on that host.

Publishing from app.localhost:3000 with a changed display name makes the very next request to the custom host show the new name without a deploy, and mara.localhost:3000 and links.example.test show the same name at the same time (shared cache tag).
Domain lookup uses a server-only query on domains and pages.published with the secret key; a lookup that hits the database error path returns 404 rather than a 500 with details.

features.title: Add a custom domain through the Vercel Domains API
acceptance: Test harness: a local Vercel API stub (set through VERCEL_API_BASE_URL) records every request (method, path, teamId, project id, Authorization header) and returns configurable responses; every domain test runs against it, never against api.vercel.com.

Pro account on http://app.localhost:3000/domains: the Custom domain card shows a labelled 'Domain' input (16px text, placeholder links.yourname.com), a labelled 'Serves' select listing the account's pages (default: the current page) and an 'Add domain' button; submitting links.example.test inserts one domains row (hostname links.example.test, page_id = chosen page, status 'pending', verified_at null), the stub receives exactly one add-project-domain request for that name carrying VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, VERCEL_TEAM_ID and the bearer token, and a domain card appears without a reload.

Server-side hostname validation (the same validator drives the inline error under the input; each case returns 400 invalid_hostname, creates no row and makes no Vercel call): https://links.example.test, links.example.test/page, links.example.test:3000, 'links example.test', *.example.test, localhost, 203.0.113.5, a_b.example.test, a name over 253 characters, a label over 63; hydlnk.com, www.hydlnk.com, mara.hydlnk.com and HYDLNK.COM; app.localhost; foo.vercel.app. Messages say what to do, for example 'Enter just the domain, like links.example.com.' and 'That is a HYDLNK address. Use a domain you own.'
Normalisation: 'LINKS.Example.Test.' is stored as links.example.test; an internationalised name such as bücher.example is stored and displayed in punycode (xn--bcher-kva.example).

Uniqueness: adding links.example.test again, from the same or another account, returns 409 hostname_taken ('That domain is already connected to a page.') with no Vercel call; a Vitest race with two simultaneous adds of the same hostname creates exactly one row.

Plan gate and ownership: a Free account's call to the server action returns 403 plan_required and the stub sees no request; a Pro account submitting another account's page id returns 403 and creates nothing. Direct-API abuse: with the owner's JWT and the publishable key, POST /rest/v1/domains {page_id, hostname:'x.example', status:'verified'} is rejected and creates no row, because add is server-only.

Vercel failures leave no orphan: a stub 5xx or an 8-second timeout on add leaves no row and shows 'We couldn’t reach our host to add that domain. Try again.'; a domain-in-use conflict leaves no row and shows 'That domain is already connected elsewhere on our host. Contact support.'; the Hobby 50-domain cap error shows 'We can’t add more domains right now. Try again later.'; a forced database error after a successful Vercel add triggers a compensating remove request to the stub.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/domains the input, select and button stack, each full width and at least 44px tall, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide), with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.

features.title: Check DNS now, live polling and the five-minute verification sweep
acceptance: On a pending domain the 'Check DNS now' button (charcoal, 44px) posts a server action that asks Vercel to verify the domain and reads its config; when Vercel reports verified and not misconfigured, the server sets status 'verified' and verified_at = now() with the secret key, the card flips to the live state in place and the button becomes 'Open links.example.test'. When Vercel reports unverified or misconfigured the row stays 'pending' and a line under the buttons reads 'Checked just now. DNS isn’t pointing here yet. Records can take a while to spread.'; the button shows 'Checking…' with aria-busy and is disabled while the request is in flight.

Cooldown: a new server-only column domains.last_checked_at is set on every check and a second check within 10 seconds returns the stored result with 'Checked a few seconds ago.'; 20 rapid POSTs to the action produce at most one Vercel verify request in 10 seconds (stub counter).

Page polling: while a pending domain is shown and the tab is visible, the page asks the server for its state every 10 seconds, backs off to every 30 seconds after 5 minutes, pauses while document.visibilityState is hidden and stops after 30 minutes; switching the stub to verified changes the chip to 'Live · SSL issued' within 15 seconds with no reload.

Sweep: POST /api/cron/verify-domains on the app host with 'Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>' verifies up to 50 pending domains created in the last 7 days, least recently checked first, using the same verify routine and cooldown, and returns JSON {checked, verified}; with two pending domains and the stub reporting one verified, one call flips exactly that row; a pending domain created 8 days earlier is skipped (it can still be verified through Check DNS now).

A migration schedules the pg_cron job 'verify-pending-domains' at '*/5 * * * *' that calls the endpoint through pg_net with the secret and base URL read from Supabase Vault; pgTAP asserts the cron.job row exists with that schedule and that its command text contains neither the secret nor a hard-coded production hostname.

Abuse case: a missing or wrong secret, or a secret passed in the query string, returns 401 (constant-time comparison) and changes nothing; GET returns 405; the route returns 404 on tenant, custom and marketing hosts; the secret never appears in the client bundle, in response bodies or in logs. With the owner's JWT and the publishable key, PATCH /rest/v1/domains?id=eq.<id> with {status:'verified'} or {verified_at:...} is rejected and the row stays pending; the check action given another account's domain id returns 404 with no Vercel call.
SSRF guard: during check, polling and the sweep the server makes requests only to the Vercel API host and never to the custom hostname itself (fetch spy and stub log).

features.title: Cookieless visitor hash with a daily rotating salt

The client IP is the first entry of x-forwarded-for, else x-real-ip, else 0.0.0.0 in local dev; a Vitest case covers each source.

features.title: View beacon records page views
acceptance: On a published page opened at http://mara.localhost:3000/ (and at the custom host) the page calls navigator.sendBeacon('/api/e', JSON string {pageId, referrer: document.referrer}) exactly once per load, after load, with a relative URL so the request goes to whichever host served the page; Playwright counts one POST per navigation in both projects (390x844 with an iPhone user agent, 1440x900 with a desktop Chrome user agent string).

The server answers 204 with Cache-Control no-store and no Set-Cookie and inserts one events row: type 'view', page_id, block_id null, ts now, referrer = the referrer's hostname lowercased with a leading 'www.' removed ('https://l.instagram.com/?u=x' becomes l.instagram.com; empty, non-http(s) or the page's own host becomes null), device mobile, tablet or desktop from the user agent (iPhone Safari mobile, iPad tablet, desktop Chrome desktop, anything unmatched desktop), country from x-vercel-ip-country as two uppercase letters else null, and visitor_hash of 64 hex characters.

Editor preview and drafts never count: opening the editor preview on http://app.localhost:3000 produces zero /api/e requests, and a published page with unpublished draft changes records views against the published version only.

Ignored with an identical 204 (no oracle) and no insert: an unknown or malformed pageId, a page with published = null, an Origin that is not that page's own origin (https://{handle}.hydlnk.com, http://{handle}.localhost:3000 in dev, or one of its verified custom hosts), and a missing Origin; a body over 2 KB returns 413 and inserts nothing.

Direct-API abuse case: with the publishable key, as anon and as a signed-in user, POST /rest/v1/events is rejected and GET /rest/v1/events returns no rows or a permission error; a forged curl beacon with the right pageId and Origin https://evil.example inserts nothing.
The public page document stays static: it sets no cookie and is identical for every visitor, the beacon being the only per-visit request, and no cookie banner appears.

features.title: Click redirect /r/[pageId]/[blockId]
acceptance: Published outbound links (link buttons, link cards, grid cells, image links and social icons with web URLs) render a relative href of /r/<pageId>/<blockId-or-item-id> on the public page, because `outboundHref()` from Milestone 2 now returns it; the social email icon keeps its mailto: href untracked; the editor preview renders the same /r hrefs (markup stays identical per Milestone 2) but its wrapper intercepts clicks, so previewing makes no /r request and logs no click.

GET http://mara.localhost:3000/r/<pageId>/<blockId> for a link block whose published URL is https://example.com/book returns 302 with Location exactly https://example.com/book and Cache-Control no-store (never 301, 307 or 308), and inserts one events row: type 'click', page_id, block_id, device, country, visitor_hash, referrer null; the response has no Set-Cookie.

The target comes only from the page's published document: a block that exists only in the draft, a block whose URL was edited in the draft but not republished (the old published URL is used), an unknown blockId, a block with no URL (text, divider), a page with published = null, and malformed ids (pageId not a uuid, blockId outside [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}) all return 404 and insert nothing; malformed ids are rejected without a database query. Link items nested inside a 2-column grid or a social row resolve by their own item ids.

Open-redirect abuse case: ?url=https://evil.example, ?to=, ?redirect=, ?next=, a different Host header and X-Forwarded-Host never change Location; a published URL whose scheme is not http or https (inserted by bypassing validation, for example javascript: or data:) returns 404 instead of redirecting.

Works with JavaScript disabled (Playwright javaScriptEnabled false: clicking the link follows the 302 to the destination) and on the custom host (links.example.test/r/...) as well as the subdomain, in both the 390x844 and 1440x900 projects.
Resilience: with a database error injected into the events insert the response is still the 302; the insert runs after the response is sent (Next after()), so the redirect does not wait for it.

features.title: Bots and HEAD requests are dropped before insert
acceptance: Vitest table: a shared isBot(userAgent) (isbot package pinned, plus an empty or missing user agent counts as a bot) returns true for Googlebot, bingbot, facebookexternalhit/1.1, Slackbot-LinkExpanding 1.0, Twitterbot/1.0, WhatsApp/2.23.20, curl/8.4.0, python-requests/2.31.0, Go-http-client/2.0 and Playwright's default HeadlessChrome user agent, and false for iPhone Safari, iPad Safari, Android Chrome and desktop Chrome.
POST /api/e with a bot user agent, a valid published pageId and a valid Origin returns 204 and inserts nothing; the same request with no User-Agent header inserts nothing.

GET /r/<pageId>/<blockId> with a bot user agent still returns the 302 to the published URL (link previews and crawlers keep working) but inserts nothing; HEAD /r/<pageId>/<blockId> returns the same status and Location with no body and inserts nothing; HEAD and GET on /api/e return 405 and insert nothing.

Humans still count: the Playwright projects set real-browser user agent strings (iPhone 13 descriptor at 390x844, a desktop Chrome string at 1440x900) so view and click assertions are not filtered; one test using the default HeadlessChrome user agent asserts zero events.
Abuse case: every case above is asserted by counting rows in events before and after through the secret-key test helper, covering both endpoints.

features.title: Nightly pg_cron rollup into daily_stats and daily_dim_stats
acceptance: Migration adds daily_dim_stats(page_id, day, dim, value, views) with primary key (page_id, day, dim, value), RLS on, and a policy letting a page's owner select its rows; pgTAP: tenant A reads its own rows, tenant B reads none of them, and neither can insert, update or delete.

rollup_daily_stats(day date) for a UTC day upserts, per page, one daily_stats row with block_id null holding views, clicks and uniques (distinct visitor_hash among views), one row per clicked block (block_id set) holding clicks, and daily_dim_stats rows for dim 'referrer' (empty becomes 'direct'), 'device' and 'country' (null becomes 'unknown') counting views; referrers beyond the top 50 per page and day fold into value 'other'.

pgTAP with synthetic events across two days, including 23:59:59 and 00:00:00 UTC: per-day sums match; running the function twice for the same day yields identical rows (idempotent, no doubling); a page with no events that day gets no rows; block rows keep their block_id after the block is removed from the published document.

rollup_recent_days(n int) rolls up the last n completed UTC days (today excluded); a migration schedules the pg_cron job 'rollup-daily-stats' at '10 0 * * *' running rollup_recent_days(3) so a missed night heals itself; pgTAP asserts the cron.job row (name, schedule, command).

Abuse case: with the publishable key, POST /rest/v1/rpc/rollup_daily_stats and rpc/rollup_recent_days are rejected for anon and authenticated (execute revoked); POST, PATCH and DELETE on daily_stats and daily_dim_stats are rejected; tenant B's select on tenant A's daily_stats returns no rows while A sees them.

features.title: Raw events are kept for 90 days

Before deleting it rolls up every day it is about to delete: with no daily_stats rows for the -91d day beforehand, rows with the correct totals exist afterwards; daily_stats and daily_dim_stats rows are never deleted by this job.

features.title: Per-IP rate limit on the view beacon /api/e, and the rate-limit mechanism decision
acceptance: Decision recorded in docs/PLAN.md (the Open item moves to Decided) naming the mechanism behind one rateLimit(key, limit, windowSeconds) function used by /api/e, /r, uploads and reports, with the reason for the choice; the mechanism must work in local dev and in Playwright, and any platform rule (e.g. a Vercel Firewall rule) is only a coarse backstop in front of it.

Vitest on rateLimit with limit 120 per 60 s: calls 1-120 for IP 203.0.113.7 are allowed, call 121 is blocked with retryAfter between 1 and 60, a call for 198.51.100.9 in the same window is allowed, and after the window rolls over 203.0.113.7 is allowed again.

Playwright API test: POST http://mara.localhost:3000/api/e with a valid view-beacon body for the seed mara page and header x-forwarded-for: 203.0.113.7, 121 times inside one minute. Requests 1-120 return 204; request 121 returns 429 with a Retry-After header and does not add an events row; the same body from 198.51.100.9 immediately afterwards returns 204.

Every request counts toward the limit, including malformed JSON bodies and bot or HEAD requests, and the limit check runs before any events insert (Vitest asserts the insert function is never called for a blocked request).

Direct-curl abuse: a request with no client-IP header is counted in one shared 'unknown' bucket instead of skipping the limit, and the key is the platform-supplied client IP, never a value taken from the beacon body. If the limiter is backed by the database, its RPC and counter table are rejected for anon and authenticated with the publishable key.
If the counter store throws, the beacon still returns 204 and the error is logged (fail open), so a limiter outage never breaks page views.

features.title: Per-IP rate limit on the click redirect /r
acceptance: Using the same rateLimit function, GET http://mara.localhost:3000/r/{pageId}/{blockId} allows 60 requests per minute per IP: requests 1-60 from 203.0.113.7 return 302 with Location equal to the block's published URL (and one click row each, bots excluded as before); request 61 returns 429 with a Retry-After header, no Location header and no new events row; the same request from 198.51.100.9 returns 302.
The limit is per IP across all pages and blocks: 30 requests to block A plus 31 to block B from one IP trip on request 61, so rotating blockIds or pageIds does not dodge it.
The 429 body is a small HYDLNK-styled page reading 'Too many clicks from your network. Try again in a minute.'. A blocked request performs no pages lookup and no events insert (Vitest spies on both).

Direct-curl abuse: GET /r/{pageId}/{blockId}?to=https://evil.example never redirects to evil.example, and a request with no client-IP header lands in the shared 'unknown' bucket rather than bypassing the limit.
If the counter store throws, the redirect still returns 302 and the error is logged (fail open): a limiter outage must never break a visitor's click.

At 1440x900 on the 429 page: it is centered and uses HYDLNK UI tokens (not tenant tokens).
